req.title: Delete post
req.statement: The system shall remove the post row and redirect to / when POST /<id>/delete is issued by the post's author.

doc.reasoning: The delete post requirement has three key behaviours to verify: (1) a logged-in author can delete their own post and is redirected to / with the row removed from the DB; (2) a non-author (or unauthenticated) user cannot delete another user's post; (3) deleting a non-existent post returns 404. I use the pre-loaded fixture data (user 1 = Rahul/stone owns posts 2,3,6,8,9,10,11,12,15,18,19,20; user 2 = Anjali/cloud owns posts 7,13,14). Tests are self-contained, use exact status codes, verify DB state, and cover mutation operators on the redirect target, the status code constants, and the DB deletion predicate.

tests.name: test_delete_post_by_author_removes_row_and_redirects
preconditions: App initialised with test DB containing pre-loaded rows
User Rahul (id=1) is logged in
Post id=2 exists and is authored by Rahul (author_id=1)
expected: Post id=2 no longer exists in the database
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import get_db

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(); os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
with app.app_context():
    from flaskr.db import init_db
    init_db()

client = app.test_client()

# Login as Rahul who owns post 2
login_r = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'Rahul', 'password': 'stone'})
assert login_r.status_code == 302

# Delete post 2
del_r = client.post('/2/delete')
assert del_r.status_code == 302
assert del_r.headers['Location'] == '/'

# Verify row is gone from DB
with app.app_context():
    db = get_db()
    row = db.execute('SELECT id FROM post WHERE id = ?', (2,)).fetchone()
    assert row is None

tests.name: test_delete_post_only_deletes_target_row
preconditions: App initialised with test DB containing pre-loaded rows
User Rahul (id=1) is logged in
Posts id=9 and id=10 both exist and are authored by Rahul
actions: Query DB for posts id=8, id=9, id=10
expected: Delete response status code is exactly 302
Post id=9 is absent from the database
trace: R-FLASKR-021: only the targeted row is removed; BVA on adjacent rows
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import get_db

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(); os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
with app.app_context():
    from flaskr.db import init_db
    init_db()

client = app.test_client()

# Login as Rahul
login_r = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'Rahul', 'password': 'stone'})
assert login_r.status_code == 302

# Delete post 9
del_r = client.post('/9/delete')
assert del_r.status_code == 302
assert del_r.headers['Location'] == '/'

with app.app_context():
    db = get_db()
    # Target row must be gone
    gone = db.execute('SELECT id FROM post WHERE id = ?', (9,)).fetchone()
    assert gone is None
    # Adjacent lower row must survive
    lower = db.execute('SELECT id FROM post WHERE id = ?', (8,)).fetchone()
    assert lower is not None
    assert lower['id'] == 8
    # Adjacent upper row must survive
    upper = db.execute('SELECT id FROM post WHERE id = ?', (10,)).fetchone()
    assert upper is not None
    assert upper['id'] == 10
